# Autumn 2025 Evening Class

My first term at Carrowmede: ten Tuesday sessions on openings and scene, 19:00 to 21:00, for 12 students.

## Outcome

Ten sessions delivered between 16 September and 9 December 2025, every student leaving with a revised opening of 1,500 to 2,500 words and one complete scene. Reached.

## Current State

- Completed 2025-12-09 with the end-of-term reading. 11 of 12 students read; one preferred not to, which is allowed.
- Fee: 10 sessions x 2 hours x 40 GBP = 800 GBP, invoiced on the December timesheet and paid 2026-01-09 ([[carrowmede-tutor-agreement-2025]]).
- Three students carried on into spring and two into autumn 2026: [[ronan-maddox]] and [[maureen-tighe]] in both, [[samir-benhaddou]] back in autumn 2026.

## Scope and Boundaries

Openings and scene only. I resisted the requests for a session on getting published; one evening in week 9 covered agents and submissions in 40 minutes and then went back to pages. Students' work is recorded only as [[student-writing-privacy-rules]] allows.

## How The Term Ran

The outline is in [[autumn-2025-course-outline]]. Broadly:

1. Sessions 1 to 3: first lines and first pages. What an opening promises. [[openings-handout-2025]] with twelve first lines, half from public-domain novels, half invented by me.
2. Sessions 4 to 6: scene as a unit of change. Each scene ends with someone in a different position than they began.
3. Sessions 7 and 8: dialogue that carries information without anyone explaining it.
4. Session 9: revision of the opening against the scene work; the publishing Q&A.
5. Session 10: reading.

Half term fell on 28 October; the centre's open evening took 21 October. Ten sessions in twelve weeks.

## What I Learned

- Two hours is short. The first half hour went on reading back last week's exercises until I capped it at three readers a week, rotating.
- A first-time tutor overprepares. I wrote eight-page handouts in September and two-page ones by November; the two-page ones were used more.
- Ronan's harbour knowledge and Maureen's reading were already the two strongest presences in the room. Samir wrote the most and revised the least, and said so himself.
- My translator's habit of line-level comment is useful one to one and deadly in a group. Group comment now goes to structure; line notes go on paper.
